newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq holds gathering in support of its POWs in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Iraq holds gathering in support of its POWs in Iran.

text.p: Hundreds of women and children demonstrated in front of a United Nations office in Baghdad on Monday to appeal for the release of Iraqi prisoners captured by Iran during the 1980-88 Gulf War.

Weeping women among the crowd carried photographs of their missing husbands and sons and raised placards urging the United Nations to act to free what Baghdad says are more than 18,000 Iraqis languishing in Iranian camps.
It was the first such demonstration in Iraq organised to crown a week of solidarity with Iraqi prisoners of war (POWs) in Iran.
"I am sure my husband is in pain now in Iran. We here spend our days in melancholy, What a life is this?" said Nawal Ibrahim, 40, mother of three.
Ibrahim said her husband was captured in 1981, two years into the eight-year war.

Most of the several hundred demonstrators were women. Some had brought their children along. Samira Hussein, 61, said the last letter she received from her only son was in 1984 and since had heard nothing.
"I want my Fadhil. I want to know whether he is dead or alive. If dead I need his remains. He is my only one, I need him desperately," she said.

Some women urged Iran in the name of Islam and Prophet Mohammed to free the POWs. "We are Moslems and you are Moslems. We all have the same prophet. In the name of Allah and Mohammed send us our sons and husbands," shouted a woman in the crowd.
The emotive gathering dispersed with two women handing a representative from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Baghdad a letter.
The POWs issue is among the thorniest blocking the normalisation of ties between the two countries. Iranian and Iraqi officials have held several meetings to solve the problem but to no avail.

Iraq says Iran still keeps 18,275 Iraqi POWs, 8,718 of them registered at the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). Information on the rest was gathered from letters they sent through the ICRC to relatives in Iraq.
Iraq says it freed 39,044 Iranian POWs in the large-scale exchange of prisoners in 1990 and denies Iranian claims of keeping any more on its territory.

The countries also have a long way to go to solve the issue of soldiers reported missing in action (MIAs). Iraq puts the number of its MIAs at 63,796. Iran has been giving conflicting figures on its POWs and MIAs.
